lede: Tuesday is the one to watch this week: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would lock new landscaping and tree standards into the Land Use Code — that's a real vote with real consequences for property owners. The same day, the Telluride Housing Authority meets to work through a thorny primary-residency question for dependents in multi-custodial households, and Thursday's Planning & Zoning session digs into three Town-owned development projects in the Accommodations 2 zone, including the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on Wildfire Resiliency Code changes to landscaping and historic review.
New policy on primary residency for dependents in split-custody households could affect deed holders.
P&Z reviews subdivision and concept plans for three Town-owned redevelopment sites.
